column1: # For each governed concept: the one operative source (or an explicit exception), the surfaces that project it,
# the historical or explanatory surfaces that mention it, the drift risk the audit found, and the treatment.
# Locators: a repository path; ci:<path> for an executable CI surface (code, not prose); github:<owner>/<repo>#<n>
# for a decision record that lives on GitHub. Lists are ;-separated. tests/test-doc-roles.sh checks every path
# exists and every projection is registered as current-projection, explanation or an operative contract.
# Columns: concept <TAB> operative source <TAB> current projections <TAB> historical / explanatory <TAB> drift risk <TAB> treatment

column5: high — every milestone's instance is restated in the roadmap and the release records, and the constitution still names a retired gate
column6: the role marker is the one definition; instances are dated projections; ROADMAP declares itself a projection; the constitution's Platform Compatibility Review paragraph is marked superseded (ADR-0026 retired it 2026-08-11)

column5: medium — the seeded-project rule (milestone declares, Release-As mints) and this repository's default bump semantics read as one rule
column6: COMPOSITE: the ownership page states the human boundary and the policy in prose, the release-please workflow executes the minting — one rule, its statement and its code; AGENTS.md now distinguishes the two and points at release-ownership.md, the boundary's one full statement

column5: medium — the crossroad definition and the non-escalatable boundary were each stated verbatim in two places
column6: COMPOSITE: the fact model defines the closed boundary and scope vocabularies (what a boundary is), routing-classes.tsv the routing consequence (the human class is not escalatable) — two authorities over two aspects, no overlap; cli.md's crossroad paragraph points at the doctrine; execution-routing.md points at the shipped cli statement

column5: high — four citations of #677 in the repository, no definition; the mechanical merge condition is fact-model R15
column6: EXCEPTION: the grant is a human decision record on GitHub (#677) and its prose home, ADR-0032, is in review in PR #727 (human-owned, untouched); nothing here may define it

column5: low since #732 — the CI lane (.github/workflows/openai-review.yml, .github/scripts/docs-truth.sh) implements the same rule in code
column6: COMPOSITE: the fact model states what a HEAD-bound fact is (R7) and what it records (R20), the freshness contract when it stops being true (F1, F7, F13) — one model, one contract, versioned together; none beyond registration; the PR-body HEAD line the audit brief assumed does not exist on master — the comment marker is the only HEAD-bound record

column5: medium — three neighbouring vocabularies (handoff states READY|CHANGES REQUIRED|PENDING|NOT ASSESSED, docs-truth results PASS|FAIL|NOT ASSESSED, bounded-execution outcomes PROCEED|STOP|ESCALATE|CONVERGED) read as the reviewer's
column6: ci-handoff.md names its vocabulary as handoff states and points at the verdict identifier; the CI scripts (.github/scripts/openai-review/lib.sh, reviewer-instructions.txt) implement the identifier and are not prose

column5: high — the issue templates asked authors to write "Blocked by #N" in the body, which the model classifies as prose that creates nothing; a pre-v0.20 baseline still says native blocked-by is not the sole authority
column6: COMPOSITE: the governance model says which relationship is the executable dependency (native blocked-by) and what prose may do, the fact model how a graph fact represents it (class graph) — meaning and representation; the templates now say prose explains and the native relationship records; the baseline carries a historical banner

column5: medium — two lanes are both called independent review: the built-in /code-review lane the validate skill orchestrates and the OpenAI reviewer lane
column6: COMPOSITE: the lane document defines the lane (advisory verdicts, at most one review per exact HEAD), the openai-review workflow executes it — statement and code of one lane; the manifest names the two review lanes; the lane document is dev-only

column5: was high — the convention preferred true merge commits with plainly titled pull requests while the v0.23 packets (#738–#740, #731, #732) landed as squash merges with conventional titles under #677
column6: COMPOSITE: the convention states the governed strategy, the ruleset what GitHub permits. DECIDED 2026-09-07 by the owner on PR #762: true merge commits are Spark's default governed merge strategy; the strategy becomes an explicit repository/operator preference, squash and rebase permitted when selected with equivalent exact-HEAD and provenance guarantees (its own work unit); the v0.23 packets already landed are the recorded exception, stated in the convention
